body.statement: Let \(p=2\), let \(\mathsf G\in\mathcal G_p\), and let \(\pi\in\Pi\) be finitely supported. If the finite curved-score certificate in \(\mathrm{def:curved-score-certificate}\) holds, then \(R(\delta_{\pi})=b(\pi)=v=q\), \(\pi\in\Pi^{\star}\), and \(\mathcal D^{\star}=\{\delta_{\pi}\}\) up to \(\lambda^p\)-almost-everywhere equality. Moreover, \(\delta_{\pi}\notin\mathcal D_1\), so \(\mathsf G\in\mathsf C_{\mathrm{none}}\). Thus exact primal-dual closure, nonvanishing of the finite Gaussian-mixture score, and one regular boundary arc with curvature bounded away from zero form a finite sufficient certificate for the no-one-index branch.
body.justification: This is the new angle's theorem-level kernel: it turns a finite-support prior, a closed global regret gap, and a local two-jet calculation into uniqueness over all measurable randomized rules and impossibility of every scalar-index representation.
body.gap: MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Decision excludes linear threshold rules only under special conditions and does not exclude arbitrary randomized one-index rules. Theorems 1--2 of AradillasFernandezMontielOleaQiuStoyeTinda2026RobustBayes characterize uniqueness, randomization, and linear-index threshold behavior for ex-ante and ex-post robust-Bayes criteria under the constrained prior class in their equation (2.9); they do not characterize the unrestricted minimax-regret saddle over all endpoint states or exclude every measurable rule of the form \(g(w^{\top}z)\). The Abstract of the corrected proof of ChristensenMoonSchorfheide2026OptimalDecisionRules states an asymptotic discrete-choice criterion that combines minimax treatment of ambiguity in the partially identified payoff parameter conditional on a point-identified parameter with average-risk minimization for that point-identified parameter. That hybrid asymptotic criterion neither implies nor is implied by exact minimax regret over every signed endpoint state, and the cited abstract makes no claim excluding every arbitrary measurable one-index rule. ZahmEtAl2020Ridge characterizes ridge approximation through projections, but not exact minimax decision correspondences or curved Gaussian-mixture Bayes boundaries.
body.consumer: A researcher can validate one finite certificate and conclude that every minimax treatment rule must use genuinely multivariate data, without searching the unrestricted rule space for alternative index representations.
